angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 54,686,194 km at 421.94 pc = 1.73 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 34088: distance 421.941 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.127), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 421.941 +/- 53.587 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 3.0729 +/- 0.2177 mas (same row, RUWE 2.78), 14.1 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 78.606 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 34088: radius 78.606 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 4497.23 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.135) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 54,686,194 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5335 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 34088: effective temperature 5335 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.116) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 34088: effective temperature 5335 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.116) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (HST/STIS Next Generation Spectral Library v2 (Heap & Lindler; MAST high-level science product), HD 52973) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 1.1 from 2023A&A...678A.195D, the median of its 125 spectra; the 143 published values span log g 0.8 to 3.41, across which the limb law changes by at most 1.9% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A%26A...678A.195D)
